Mala Seydemynukha Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kherson Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Mala Seydemynukha carries a genuinely unique distinction: founded in 1841 as an offshoot Jewish agricultural colony from the original settlement of Seydemenukha — Hebrew for 'Field of Repose' — it is described as the only place in modern Ukraine to retain a Hebrew-derived name, even after being renamed Shterndorf in 1929 and reverting, with a slight spelling change, to its current form in 1944. Its Jewish population reached an extraordinary 97 percent by 1897. On September 17, 1941, about 340 of the colony's Jews were murdered.
